title: Speed camera penalties, Erb's Road shelter and budget rules
subtitle: Racism delegations, Wilmot land assembly concerns, Eagle Street purchases, grants policy, Scheifele Bridge expropriation and winter shelter planning
overview: Regional Council adopted an administrative penalty program for automated speed enforcement, with its hearing officer bylaw and policy {{vote:m6}}. It also adopted a warrant process for designating Community Safety Zones, including at school zones that will get speed cameras {{vote:m5}}. Supporters said speeding is avoidable and the program can be adjusted later. Opponents said the doubled fines burden low-income households.

Council voted to keep funding the Erb's Road Hybrid Emergency Shelter until at least 2030, or as long as it is needed {{vote:m7}}. Council also approved a grants policy overhaul, a December 2 deadline for budget amendment motions {{vote:m8}}, and the purchase of two Eagle Street properties in Cambridge for housing {{vote:m9}}.

Several delegates spoke about rising racism in the region, and council asked for a report on education and action items. Other delegates opposed or supported the Wilmot land assembly. A deferred motion on the land assembly was withdrawn after a closed session. Staff outlined winter shelter plans, and the King Street shelter is scheduled to close at the end of March.

decisions.detail: Council enacted the Administrative Penalty Program Bylaw and the Hearing Officer Bylaw and approved the hearing officer appointment and conduct policy {{vote:m6}}.
Council adopted a two-step warrant for Community Safety Zones and a strategy of designating them at all future speed camera school zones, and directed staff to report back with lists and options.

decisions.item: Erb's Road shelter and homelessness plan
decisions.detail: Council endorsed prioritizing the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness, committed to fund the Erb's Road shelter until at least 2030, and directed staff to seek a six-month wastewater extension from Wilmot's chief building official.
Council changed grants administration so Council approves streams while staff administer them, and set a December 2 written-notice deadline for motions to amend the final budget.

Council authorized buying 134 and 136 Eagle Street South, Cambridge, for $675,000 each, with debenture financing in the housing capital program and about $129,000 in the draft 2025 housing operating budget.

Council approved expropriation steps for the Scheifele Bridge replacement, a septic incentive program, the Franklin Boulevard design, business support programs and bus procurement considering all propulsion options.
Council ratified Rachel Zhang's appointment to the Sunnyside Foundation Board for a term ending September 2027.

debate: On speed camera fines, one councillor said doubling them puts pressure on people already struggling, noting food insecurity affects many families. Another said the 24-hour enforcement and the focus on speeders overreach, as school-area collisions are often caused by turning or backing vehicles.

Supporters said the doubling is required by provincial legislation, that residents want less speeding, and that Council can adjust the program later. One councillor noted that fines can be cancelled or made payable over time for those who cannot pay.

On Erb's Road, one councillor said emergency shelters are not the problem and the region should invest in permanent housing first, noting 40 residents have no next step. Others said it is not either/or and cited cost comparisons and housing outcomes. A heated exchange followed about criticism of staff and a councillor's newspaper op-ed.

Delegates on racism asked for an anti-racism campaign with area municipalities, better data collection and wider community involvement. Councillors expressed support and asked for a report with action items.

Delegates on the Wilmot land assembly split. A business group said a large site is needed to attract and keep major employers. Environmental and farmland delegates cited the secrecy, vacant industrial land, groundwater and farmland loss.
